description: Residential Energy Demand Temperature Index is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. Explore data showing year-to-year fluctuations in energy demand for residential heating and cooling. The Residential Energy Demand Temperature Index (REDTI) is based on population-weighted heating and cooling degree days. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat. Assets: Energy and Utilities, People. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
